studies.citation: Gsell AS, Scharfenberger U, Özkundakci D, Walters A, Hansson L-A, Janssen ABG et al. (2016) Evaluating early-warning indicators of critical transitions in natural aquatic ecosystems. PNAS 113(50):E8089–E8095
studies.data_system: Long-term monitoring datasets of FIVE freshwater ecosystems with documented sudden, persistent transitions (search results say five, not nine); Lake Mendota is mentioned in a later citing paper. Specific lake list not visible in search results.
studies.outcome_definition: Sudden, persistent transitions in state variables hypothesized to represent critical transitions, with 'well understood' mechanisms and drivers; a citing paper describes the evaluation as EWI behaviour 'prior to identified breakpoints in state variable time series'.
studies.baseline_comparator: none visible in search results (indicator trends assessed relative to identified breakpoints; no state/trend forecasting baseline visible)
studies.key_finding: Four common EWIs (SD, AR1, density ratio, skewness) 'could be detected in most of the case studies' but agreement among indicators was low; in some cases EWIs appeared considerably ahead of the transition; authors conclude EWIs 'do not provide reliable and consistent signals of impending critical transitions' even in some of the best routinely monitored freshwater ecosystems.
studies.notes: The orchestrator label 'nine lakes' is NOT supported by search results; PNAS/PubMed/KNAW snippets all say five freshwater ecosystems. All five systems were selected for having transitions, so no non-transitioning ecosystems appear to be included; whether within-series null windows were used is not visible. Retrospective, breakpoint-anchored analysis.

studies.citation: O'Brien DA et al. (2023) Early warning signals have limited applicability to empirical lake data. Nature Communications 14 (published 1 Dec 2023); preprint title: 'Early warning signals are hampered by a lack of critical transitions in empirical lake data' (bioRxiv 2023.05.11.540304)
studies.data_system: Multi-trophic planktonic (phytoplankton and zooplankton) monitoring data on multiple lakes worldwide; lakes named in snippets include Lake Kinneret, the Zurich lakes, Windermere, Lake Washington, Lake Mendota. Number of lakes not visible in search results.
studies.outcome_definition: Each lake/trophic-level series classified as critical transition (breakpoint matched in environmental state space plus hysteresis evidence, e.g. non-overlapping clusters after driver relaxation), abrupt non-bifurcation shift (breakpoint present but state-space/hysteresis criteria not met, e.g. Lake Washington zooplankton), or non-transition (e.g. Windermere phytoplankton).
studies.baseline_comparator: chance (0.5 probability); no state/trend forecasting baseline visible
studies.key_finding: Few instances of true critical transitions; different trophic levels often express different forms of abrupt change. Reliability evaluated separately on 'true positive' (transitioning) and 'true negative' (non-transitioning) series at monthly and yearly resolution: no indicator exceeded 0.5 reliability across scenarios; eigenMAF was best (monthly-true 0.62; yearly-true 0.70; monthly-false 0.49; yearly-false 0.52). Most indicators no better than chance; multivariate EWSs weakly superior to univariate; a recent machine-learning model performed poorly; results 'highly processing dependent'.
studies.notes: Directly relevant precedent: explicitly scores EWS performance on non-transitioning series (true negatives). Whether indicators were computed in expanding/rolling windows with sequential origins is not visible in search results. Note the ML model evaluated is presumably out-of-sample by construction but details not visible.

studies.citation: Burthe SJ et al. (2016) Do early warning indicators consistently predict nonlinear change in long-term ecological data? Journal of Applied Ecology 53:666–676
studies.data_system: Long-term abundance time series of 55 taxa (126 data sets) across multiple trophic levels in marine and freshwater ecosystems, including Isle of May (Scotland) seabirds and North Sea plankton (phytoplankton/zooplankton important in sandeel diets).
studies.outcome_definition: Significant nonlinear change in abundance ('turning points') identified by fitting generalized additive models (GAMs) to standardized abundance data.
studies.baseline_comparator: none visible in search results (classification of series into true/false positives/negatives; no state/trend forecasting baseline)
studies.key_finding: Time series containing true positives were uncommon (8% for variance; 6% for autocorrelation), with all but one time series also containing false classifications; 43% of series categorized differently by variance vs autocorrelation; little temporal synchrony of turning points across taxa/trophic levels. Authors conclude variance and autocorrelation 'consistently fail to predict nonlinear change' and recommend multivariate, driver-informed, process-based approaches.
studies.notes: Explicitly scores false positives at the series level (EWI present, no turning point), which the intended novelty statement must acknowledge. Retrospective design; turning points and indicator trends assessed over whole series rather than at sequential forecast origins.

studies.citation: Carpenter SR et al. (2011) Early warnings of regime shifts: a whole-ecosystem experiment. Science 332(6033):1079–1082
studies.data_system: Whole-lake experiment: Peter Lake (Michigan/Wisconsin UNDERC) manipulated by gradually adding largemouth bass over 3 years; adjacent Paul Lake monitored as unmanipulated reference.
studies.outcome_definition: Experimentally induced food-web regime shift (transition to piscivore dominance / trophic cascade); 'completion' of the food web transition used as the reference event.
studies.baseline_comparator: unmanipulated reference lake (Paul Lake), which 'revealed baseline variability but showed no trends'; no state/trend forecasting baseline
studies.key_finding: Statistical warning signals (slowing return rates, rising variance and related indicators) were evident in the manipulated lake during food-web reorganization more than a year before the transition was complete, corroborating theory; described as first experimental field evidence.
studies.notes: n=1 manipulated ecosystem plus 1 reference; false alarms handled qualitatively via the reference lake rather than as a quantified rate. Whether indicators were computed prospectively during the experiment is not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Seekell DA, Carpenter SR, Cline TJ, Pace ML (2012) Conditional heteroskedasticity forecasts regime shift in a whole-ecosystem experiment. Ecosystems 15:751–757
studies.data_system: Same Peter (manipulated) / Paul (reference) whole-lake experiment; chlorophyll-a and fish-catch time series.
studies.outcome_definition: Experimentally induced food-web regime shift (as in Carpenter et al. 2011).
studies.baseline_comparator: adjacent unmanipulated reference lake; no state/trend forecasting baseline
studies.key_finding: Moving-window conditional heteroskedasticity tests showed significant CH at least a year before the regime shift in the manipulated lake and no significant CH in the reference lake.
studies.notes: Moving-window tests are sequential in form but evaluation is retrospective; false positives addressed only via absence of significance in the single reference lake.

studies.citation: Batt RD, Carpenter SR, Cole JJ, Pace ML, Johnson RA (2013) Changes in ecosystem resilience detected in automated measures of ecosystem metabolism during a whole-lake manipulation. PNAS 110(43)
studies.data_system: 4-year whole-lake manipulation (piscivorous bass slowly added to a planktivore-dominated lake) with a nearby bass-dominated lake as unmanipulated reference; automated high-frequency sensors (DO, pH, chlorophyll-a) and derived GPP/R/NEP.
studies.outcome_definition: Completion of transition to piscivore dominance (trophic cascade) in the manipulated lake.
studies.baseline_comparator: unmanipulated reference lake; no state/trend forecasting baseline
studies.key_finding: Thresholds detected in some automated sensor measurements more than a year before completion of the transition; directly measured variables (DO, pH, chl-a) were better indicators than estimated metabolic rates.
studies.notes: Reference lake provides a non-transitioning comparison but no false-alarm rate is visible in search results.

studies.citation: Cline TJ, Seekell DA, Carpenter SR, Pace ML, Hodgson JR, Kitchell JF, Weidel BC (2014) Early warnings of regime shifts: evaluation of spatial indicators from a whole-ecosystem experiment. Ecosphere 5(8)
studies.data_system: Same whole-lake manipulation (transition to predator dominance); spatial statistics of ecosystem properties.
studies.outcome_definition: Previously documented whole-lake transition to predator dominance, 'a type of critical transition'.
studies.key_finding: First test of spatial early-warning statistics (spatial variance/autocorrelation analogues) using a deliberate whole-ecosystem field manipulation; quantitative results not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Spatial, not temporal, indicators; results beyond framing not visible.

studies.citation: Wilkinson GM, Carpenter SR, Cole JJ, Pace ML, Batt RD, Buelo CD, Kurtzweil JT (2018) Early warning signals precede cyanobacterial blooms in multiple whole-lake experiments. Ecological Monographs 88(2):188–203
studies.data_system: Six whole-lake experimental nutrient additions (UNDERC experimental lakes) to induce the clear-water to cyanobacteria-dominated regime shift.
studies.outcome_definition: Regime shift from clear-water state to cyanobacteria-dominated state (bloom) following nutrient enrichment.
studies.baseline_comparator: not visible in search results (reference-lake handling and alarm thresholds not visible)
studies.key_finding: Title-level claim that early warning signals preceded cyanobacterial blooms across six whole-lake nutrient-addition experiments; in one experiment fertilization was halted in response to detected early warnings (increased autocorrelation).
studies.notes: Search snippets did not expose the reference-lake design, alarm thresholds, or any false-positive accounting for this paper; treat design fields as unknown rather than absent.

studies.citation: Pace ML et al. (2017) Reversal of a cyanobacterial bloom in response to early warnings. PNAS 114
studies.data_system: Whole-lake experiment: Peter Lake gradually nutrient-enriched while reference lakes were monitored; a separate continuously enriched lake served as comparison.
studies.outcome_definition: Cyanobacterial bloom (algal pigments, DO saturation, pH) in the enriched lake; alarm defined as resilience indicators (variance, autocorrelation) exceeding preset boundaries.
studies.baseline_comparator: unenriched reference lakes plus a continuously enriched lake; no state/trend forecasting baseline
studies.key_finding: When resilience indicators exceeded preset boundaries, nutrient enrichment was stopped; pigments, DO saturation and pH then rapidly declined to resemble the unenriched lake, while a large bloom occurred in the continuously enriched lake. Demonstrates a prospective, real-time alarm with pre-specified thresholds in the field.
studies.notes: The only study found in this sweep with a genuinely prospective, pre-specified alarm threshold applied sequentially in real time; but n=1 managed lake and thresholds were 'preset', with the calibration basis not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Butitta VL, Carpenter SR, Loken LC, Pace ML, Stanley EH (2017) Spatial early warning signals in a lake manipulation. Ecosphere 8(10):e01941
studies.data_system: Experimental lake with nutrient-induced cyanobacteria bloom; fine-resolution spatial mapping of cyanobacteria with a mobile sensor platform.
studies.outcome_definition: Cyanobacteria bloom induced by nutrient addition.
studies.key_finding: Theoretically predicted spatial early-warning indicators based on spatial variance and spatial autocorrelation were detected prior to the bloom.
studies.notes: Spatial indicators; whether a reference lake was mapped is not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Batt RD, Eason T, Garmestani A (2019) Time scale of resilience loss: implications for managing critical transitions in water quality. PLOS ONE 14(10):e0223366
studies.data_system: Simulated lake-eutrophication model time series plus high-frequency chlorophyll fluorescence from an unmanipulated reference lake and a lake undergoing experimental fertilization.
studies.outcome_definition: Algal bloom development (critical transition) in the fertilized lake.
studies.baseline_comparator: unmanipulated reference lake; no state/trend forecasting baseline
studies.key_finding: Autocorrelation increased exponentially approaching bloom development and the manipulated-minus-reference difference in autocorrelation increased sharply; dynamics were similar across time scales, suggesting autocorrelation is robust to analysis time scale as an indicator.
studies.notes: Addresses temporal-resolution sensitivity of AR1 in lakes; relevant to the monthly vs annual resolution issue raised by O'Brien et al. 2023.

studies.citation: Buelo CD et al. (2022) Evaluating the performance of temporal and spatial early warning statistics of algal blooms. Ecological Applications 32(5):e2616
studies.data_system: Compiled time series from whole-lake experiments with and without nutrient additions (Peter Lake manipulated, Paul Lake reference), used to evaluate temporal EWS under changing vs constant resilience; data and code in an R package on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.5874868).
studies.outcome_definition: Algal (cyanobacterial) bloom in lake-years with nutrient addition; lake-years without additions treated as non-bloom (constant resilience) controls.
studies.baseline_comparator: false-positive alarm rate in lake-years not being pushed toward a bloom; no state/trend forecasting baseline visible
studies.key_finding: True-positive alarm rates were 2.5–8.3 times higher for rolling-window standard deviation when a lake was being pushed toward a bloom than the false-positive rate when it was not; for rolling-window autocorrelation alarm rates were much lower and no variable had a higher true-positive than false-positive rate. Authors conclude temporal EWS provide advance warning of blooms.
studies.notes: Closest lake-experiment precedent to an explicit alarm-rate / false-positive comparison, but limited to two experimental lakes and with no threshold calibration to a common false-alarm budget visible.

studies.citation: Wang R, Dearing JA, Langdon PG, Zhang E, Yang X, Dakos V, Scheffer M (2012) Flickering gives early warning signals of a critical transition to a eutrophic lake state. Nature 492:419–422
studies.data_system: Lake Erhai (Yunnan, China): dated sediment cores (diatom microfossils and geochemistry) reconstructing water quality back to the 1880s, plus recent monitoring; compared with model output.
studies.outcome_definition: Critical transition to a eutrophic state around 2001, interpreted as a bistable system with flickering (observed eutrophication events and blooms 1980–2000).
studies.baseline_comparator: none (single transitioning lake; model output used for qualitative comparison)
studies.key_finding: Rising variance coupled with decreasing autocorrelation and skewness began 10–30 years before the transition in both empirical records and model output, consistent with flickering rather than critical slowing down; flickering observable up to ~20 years before the transition.
studies.notes: Search results note subsequent critiques of the data-processing methods (e.g., a 2013 blog 'Flickering diatoms?'). Single-case, retrospective, selected on a known transition.

studies.citation: Doncaster CP, Alonso Chávez V, Viguier C, Wang R, Zhang E, Dong X, Dearing JA, Langdon PG, Dyke JG (2016) Early warning of critical transitions in biodiversity from compositional disorder. Ecology 97:3079–3090
studies.data_system: Lake Erhai sediment records of diatom and chironomid communities.
studies.outcome_definition: Critical transition identified around 2001 in Lake Erhai.
studies.key_finding: Proposes community-composition indicators: keystone / weedy / canary functional categories; early demise of 'canary' species and changes in compositional disorder presage critical transitions under environmental forcing, illustrated with Erhai diatoms and chironomids.
studies.notes: Community-composition (not variance/AC) indicator; single-lake retrospective case.

studies.citation: Spanbauer TL, Allen CR, Angeler DG, Eason T, Fritz SC, Garmestani AS, Nash KL, Stone JR (2014) Prolonged instability prior to a regime shift. PLoS ONE
studies.data_system: Foy Lake (Montana) sediment core: percent abundances of 109 diatom species sampled at ~5–20 year intervals, ~7,000-year record with 800 time steps.
studies.outcome_definition: Regime shift in the diatom community coinciding with regional climate change, identified with Fisher Information and multivariate time-series modelling.
studies.key_finding: Approximately 2,000-year period of instability preceded the regime shift; classical EWS (rising variance, skewness, kurtosis, lag-1 autocorrelation) were tested alongside Fisher Information; transitional periods may be far longer than typically assumed.
studies.notes: DOI not visible in search results; PMC URL used. Palaeo, single-core, retrospective.

studies.citation: Spanbauer TL, Allen CR, Angeler DG, Eason T, Fritz SC, Garmestani AS, Nash KL, Stone JR, Stow CA, Sundstrom SM (2016) Body size distributions signal a regime shift in a lake ecosystem. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 283(1833):20160249
studies.data_system: Foy Lake (Montana) ~7,000-year palaeoecological diatom record; diatom body-size distributions.
studies.outcome_definition: Major regime shift in Foy Lake biological communities attributed to climate change (previously identified).
studies.key_finding: Bayesian CART discontinuity analysis found a significant change in diatom body-size distributions ~150 years before the identified regime shift; proposed as an addition to the EWS toolkit.
studies.notes: Note the orchestrator/seed listed this as Ecosphere; search results place it in Proc R Soc B.

studies.citation: Taranu ZE et al. (2018) Can we detect ecosystem critical transitions and signals of changing resilience from paleo-ecological records? Ecosphere 9:e02438
studies.data_system: Simulated core records plus real sedimentary cyanobacterial pigment profiles from oligotrophic to hypereutrophic lakes (used to set environmental-noise coefficients of variation).
studies.outcome_definition: Regime shifts and critical transitions in simulated/real sediment records detected with time-varying autoregressions (dynamic linear models, TVARSS state-space models).
studies.baseline_comparator: simulations with known dynamics; no state/trend forecasting baseline
studies.key_finding: Smoothing inherent in palaeo records interferes with rolling-window indicators (especially autocorrelation); online DLM/TVARSS can detect regime shifts and critical transitions when signal-to-noise is strong but have limitations when records are noisy.
studies.notes: Author list beyond Taranu not visible in search results. 'Online' DLM implies sequential estimation, hence partial for time-indexed origins.

studies.citation: Su H, Wang R, Feng Y, Li Y, Li Y, Chen J, Xu C, Wang S, Fang J, Xie P (2021) Long-term empirical evidence, early warning signals and multiple drivers of regime shifts in a lake ecosystem. Journal of Ecology 109:3182–3194
studies.data_system: A subtropical Chinese lake in the Yangtze floodplain (name not visible in search results): 64-year multi-trophic monitoring plus palaeo-diatom records.
studies.outcome_definition: Catastrophic regime shifts (critical transition and hysteresis) under combined warming, eutrophication and fish-stocking trophic cascade, cross-validated by monitoring and palaeo records; both collapse and recovery trajectories examined.
studies.key_finding: EWSs reported as detectable in both the collapse and recovery trajectories; including body-size information in composite EWSs was reported to require shorter time series and improve predictive ability.
studies.notes: Single-lake retrospective case; quantitative indicator details not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Rohde E, Pearce NJT, Young J, Xenopoulos MA (2022) Applying early warning indicators to predict critical transitions in a lake undergoing multiple changes. Ecological Applications 32(7):e2685
studies.data_system: Lake Simcoe (Ontario) long-term monitoring 1980–2019, fortnightly in ice-free season; 15 state variables (DOC, phosphorus, chlorophyll-a, Secchi, silica, etc.) and multivariate-derived series at three stations (shallow, mid-depth, deep).
studies.outcome_definition: Statistical breakpoints in state-variable time series; lake transitioned from algal-dominated toward clearer, lower-nutrient state coincident with management and dreissenid mussel invasion.
studies.baseline_comparator: none visible (agreement between EWI trends and breakpoints assessed retrospectively)
studies.key_finding: Retrospective evaluation of agreement between SD, autocorrelation, skewness, kurtosis and breakpoints: Secchi depth at deep-water stations showed expected indicator trends before breakpoints, whereas total phosphorus and chlorophyll-a showed more nuanced patterns.
studies.notes: Multiple variables/stations allow implicit comparison of variables with and without breakpoints, but no explicit false-alarm rate is visible.

studies.citation: Litzow MA, Hunsicker ME (2016) Early warning signals, nonlinearity, and signs of hysteresis in real ecosystems. Ecosphere 7:e01614
studies.data_system: Review and meta-analysis of published empirical EWS studies plus comparative analysis of eight northeast Pacific Ocean time series.
studies.outcome_definition: Published ecological transitions classified by whether nonlinearity/hysteresis in dynamics was demonstrated.
studies.key_finding: Published studies demonstrating nonlinearity in ecosystem dynamics were more likely to support EWS predictions than studies with linear or undetermined dynamics; recommends restricting EWS application to transitions expected to be nonlinear.
studies.notes: Marine community focus; useful for the 'grouped by biological system' rationale.

studies.citation: Wouters N, Dakos V, Edwards M, Serafim MP, Valayer PJ, Cabral HN (2015) Evidencing a regime shift in the North Sea using early-warning signals as indicators of critical transitions. Estuarine, Coastal and Shelf Science 152:65–72
studies.data_system: North Sea community/ecosystem time series (details not visible in search results).
studies.outcome_definition: Periods of high regime-shift likelihood inferred from EWS: 1962–1972, 1989–1999, and 2002 onward.
studies.key_finding: Uses EWS to infer three periods of elevated regime-shift likelihood in parts of the North Sea.
studies.notes: DOI not visible; ScienceDirect URL used. Marine community; EWS used as evidence of shifts rather than evaluated against independently defined outcomes.

studies.citation: Drake JM, Griffen BD (2010) Early warning signals of extinction in deteriorating environments. Nature 467:456–459
studies.data_system: Laboratory Daphnia magna populations: 60 tanks, 30 with gradually reduced food (deteriorating) and 30 with stable food (controls).
studies.outcome_definition: Population extinction/collapse under deteriorating environment.
studies.baseline_comparator: control (stable-environment) populations; no state/trend forecasting baseline
studies.key_finding: Four statistical measures of abundance showed critical slowing down in degraded but not in control populations.
studies.notes: Laboratory population study with explicit non-transitioning controls; the design template for control-vs-treatment EWS comparison.

studies.citation: Veraart AJ, Faassen EJ, Dakos V, van Nes EH, Lürling M, Scheffer M (2012) Recovery rates reflect distance to a tipping point in a living system. Nature 481:357–359
studies.data_system: Cyanobacterial population microcosm (chemostat) driven to a photoinhibition tipping point by light level.
studies.outcome_definition: Classical tipping point (collapse) when a critical light level is exceeded.
studies.key_finding: Recovery from small perturbations slowed as the system approached the critical point, and autocorrelation of fluctuations rose; authors note stochasticity prohibits predicting timing but indicators may rank systems from resilient to fragile.
studies.notes: Author list partially inferred from snippet ('Veraart, A., Faassen, E., Dakos, V. et al.'); full list beyond that not visible.

studies.citation: Cerini F, Jackson J, O'Brien D, Childs DZ, Clements CF (2025) Multivariate signals of population collapse in a high-throughput ecological experiment. Ecology 106:e70197
studies.data_system: Autonomously monitored high-throughput laboratory populations of Paramecium caudatum forced to collapse by gradual pollutant introduction; individual-based behaviour, morphology and abundance data.
studies.outcome_definition: Population collapse/extinction under increasing stress.
studies.key_finding: Gradual pollutant introduction elicited a predictable sequence: declines in movement speed, then body length, then emergence of abundance-based EWS of collapse, then abundance declines.
studies.notes: Same group as O'Brien et al. 2023; demonstrates trait-based leading indicators in a lab community context.

studies.citation: Clements CF, Drake JM, Griffiths JI, Ozgul A (2015) Factors influencing the detectability of early warning signals of population collapse. American Naturalist 186(1):50–58
studies.data_system: Experimental/laboratory population data with imposed temporal and spatial subsampling (observation error); details of source data not visible in search results.
studies.outcome_definition: Population collapse (critical slowing down before collapse).
studies.key_finding: Sampling only a portion of space significantly diminished detectability of critical slowing down, whereas reducing temporal sampling frequency had much smaller effects.
studies.notes: Relevant to monitoring-design sensitivity of EWS in wild populations.

studies.citation: Boettiger C, Hastings A (2012) Early warning signals and the prosecutor's fallacy. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 279(1748):4734–4739
studies.data_system: Stochastic simulations conditionally selected on having transitioned by chance.
studies.outcome_definition: Simulated stochastic transitions (e.g., lake eutrophication analogues).
studies.key_finding: Selecting systems for study because a transition was observed (rather than forecasting prospectively) produces spurious rises in variance and autocorrelation purely from conditional selection of chance transitions ('prosecutor's fallacy'); mining historical cases can yield false positives rather than valid benchmarks.
studies.notes: Methodological foundation for requiring prospective, non-conditioned evaluation with non-transitioning series; directly motivates the time-indexed hindcast design. Companion paper 'Quantifying limits to detection of early warning for critical transitions' (J R Soc Interface 2012) surfaced in results (PubMed 22593100) but details not visible.

studies.citation: Dakos V et al. (2012) Methods for detecting early warnings of critical transitions in time series illustrated using simulated ecological data. PLoS ONE 7(7):e41010
studies.data_system: Simulated time series of systems undergoing critical transitions.
studies.outcome_definition: Simulated bifurcation-driven transitions.
studies.key_finding: Comparative toolbox of metric-based (rolling-window AR1, SD, skewness, etc.) and model-based EWS methods applied to simulated data; the standard reference implementation for the classical EWS score.
studies.notes: Defines the conventional rolling-window/Kendall-tau EWS procedure that the study's prespecified EWS score will mirror.

studies.citation: Dakos V, Carpenter SR, van Nes EH, Scheffer M (2015) Resilience indicators: prospects and limitations for early warnings of regime shifts. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 370(1659):20130263
studies.data_system: Review.
studies.outcome_definition: n/a (review)
studies.key_finding: Review of critical-slowing-down indicators (rising temporal correlation and variance) as early warnings, with discussion of prospects and limitations.
studies.notes: Background synthesis by the core EWS theory group.

studies.citation: Hastings A, Wysham DB (2010) Regime shifts in ecological systems can occur with no warning. Ecology Letters 13(4):464–472
studies.data_system: Theoretical ecological models.
studies.outcome_definition: Model regime shifts (non-bifurcation / non-smooth-potential dynamics).
studies.key_finding: The class of ecological systems expected to exhibit leading indicators is limited; a set of models exists for which regime shifts occur with no forewarning.
studies.notes: Theoretical basis for expecting false negatives in populations whose collapses are not bifurcation-driven.

studies.citation: Perretti CT, Munch SB (2012) Regime shift indicators fail under noise levels commonly observed in ecological systems. Ecological Applications 22(6):1772–1779
studies.data_system: Simulated data with noise levels matched to real ecological data.
studies.outcome_definition: Simulated regime shifts.
studies.key_finding: Early warning indicators performed poorly when simulated data had noise levels similar to those in real ecological data.
studies.notes: DOI not visible in search results; JSTOR URL used.

studies.citation: Spears BM, Futter MN, Jeppesen E, Huser BJ, Ives S, Davidson TA et al. (2017) Ecological resilience in lakes and the conjunction fallacy. Nature Ecology & Evolution 1:1616–1624
studies.data_system: Perspective using lakes as model case studies for resilience theory.
studies.outcome_definition: n/a (perspective)
studies.key_finding: Argues lake resilience research has blurred intuitive and extensional logic (conjunction fallacy) and calls for more rigorous logic before translating resilience/EWS results into management.
studies.notes: Useful framing for why strict outcome definitions and base rates matter in lakes.

studies.citation: Spears BM, Carvalho L, Futter MN, May L, Thackeray SJ, Adrian R et al. (2016) Ecological instability in lakes: a predictable condition? Environmental Science & Technology 50(7):3285–3286
studies.data_system: Viewpoint synthesizing three approaches: pressure thresholds from large lake populations, long-term data on past events, and high-frequency monitoring with statistical stability analogues.
studies.outcome_definition: n/a (viewpoint)
studies.key_finding: Frames the practical need for early detection of lake instability and cites evidence (e.g., Erhai) that indicator changes began 10–30 years before eutrophic transitions.
studies.notes: Short viewpoint piece.

studies.citation: Authors not visible in search results (2021) Early warning signals of regime shifts for aquatic systems: Can experiments help to bridge the gap between theory and real-world application? Ecological Complexity
studies.data_system: Systematic review of 119 EWS observations from 19 unique aquatic experiments, from highly controlled microcosms to whole-system manipulations.
studies.outcome_definition: Experimentally induced regime shifts/tipping points in aquatic systems.
studies.key_finding: Variance, autocorrelation, skewness and recovery rate showed a high success rate in aquatic EWS experiments; notes that identifying false positives/negatives (EWS present but no regime shift) is a critical challenge tied to response-variable relevance and low signal-to-noise; calls for experiments closer to real-world conditions.
studies.notes: Author list not visible in search results (Uppsala DiVA record suggests Swedish affiliation). Useful tabulation of experimental precedents.

studies.citation: Gsell AS, Teurlincx S, Adrian R, Janssen ABG (2023) Timing matters: sampling frequency for early-warning indicators across food web components in a virtual lake. Ecological Indicators 153:110424
studies.data_system: Simulated ('virtual') shallow lake food-web model.
studies.outcome_definition: Shallow-lake shift between clear and turbid states in the simulation.
studies.key_finding: Examines how sampling frequency affects EWI detectability across food-web components in a simulated shallow lake, motivated by managers' need for resilience-loss predictors.
studies.notes: DOI not visible; ScienceDirect URL used. Simulation-only; relevant to choosing monitoring resolution.

studies.citation: Arani BMS, Carpenter SR, Lahti L, van Nes EH, Scheffer M (2021) Exit time as a measure of ecological resilience. Science 372
studies.data_system: Examples including lake cyanobacterial (phytoplankton pigment) data; related work uses 5-minute automated measurements from whole-lake experiments.
studies.outcome_definition: Threshold crossing between alternate states (mean exit time).
studies.key_finding: Proposes mean exit time (time to cross a threshold) as a resilience measure, applied to lake cyanobacteria data.
studies.notes: Note: published in Science, not Nature (the seed query mislabelled it). Alternative resilience metric, not a variance/AC EWS.

studies.citation: Davidson TA, Sayer CD, Jeppesen E et al. (2023) Bimodality and alternative equilibria do not help explain long-term patterns in shallow lake chlorophyll-a. Nature Communications 14
studies.data_system: 902 shallow lakes (Denmark and north-eastern USA) plus simulations.
studies.outcome_definition: Tests for bimodality/alternative equilibria in chlorophyll-a vs nutrient relationships.
studies.key_finding: Shallow-lake chlorophyll-a vs nutrient relationships did not fit alternative-stable-state theory; real data matched simulations lacking alternative equilibria.
studies.notes: Relevant to the challenge analysis: many lake 'regime shifts' may not be bifurcations, consistent with O'Brien et al. 2023.

studies.citation: Authors not visible in search results (2017) Rising variance and abrupt shifts of subfossil chironomids due to eutrophication in a deep sub-alpine lake. Aquatic Ecology 51
studies.data_system: High-resolution subfossil chironomid record from a sediment core, Lake Remoray (France).
studies.outcome_definition: Abrupt shift in chironomid composition triggered by collapse of dominant Sergentia coracina-type around 1980, attributed to deep-water oxygen depletion from eutrophication.
studies.key_finding: Rising variance reported preceding an abrupt compositional shift in a benthic community (title-level claim).
studies.notes: Single-core palaeo case; author list not visible.

studies.citation: Authors not visible in search results (2019) Systematically false positives in early warning signal analysis. PLOS ONE
studies.data_system: not visible in search results
studies.outcome_definition: not visible in search results
studies.key_finding: Title indicates systematic false positives arise in EWS analysis; content not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Surfaced only as a title in the Entropy-review query; flagged for follow-up because it bears directly on the false-alarm-budget rationale.

studies.citation: Authors not visible in search results (2026) Early Warning Signals in Ecological Time-Series. Entropy 28(6):628
studies.data_system: Review spanning lakes, coral reefs, grasslands, forests and marine systems.
studies.outcome_definition: n/a (review)
studies.key_finding: Synthesis (published June 2026) arguing neither presence nor direction of indicator trends is universal: 'critical speeding up' occurs under some potential geometries and mechanism-specific false positives arise under N-, R- and S-tipping; reviews model-based and ML approaches and where empirical EWS have succeeded, failed or been ambiguous.
studies.notes: Most recent synthesis found; worth citing for the state-of-the-art review of empirical validation across ecosystem types.

studies.citation: Authors not visible in search results (2025) Navigating tipping points: a complex systems framework for anticipating lake ecosystem collapse. Journal not visible (ScienceDirect PII S2667325825003346)
studies.data_system: Review of lake ecosystems as complex adaptive systems.
studies.outcome_definition: n/a (review)
studies.key_finding: Reviews temporal, spatial and network-based indicators for lake tipping points and states that their application 'requires context-specific validation' because lakes respond heterogeneously to stressors.
studies.notes: Review only; journal and authors not visible.

studies.citation: Litzow MA et al. (2013) Rising catch variability preceded historical fisheries collapses in Alaska. Ecological Applications
studies.data_system: Historical Alaskan fisheries catch records (details not visible).
studies.outcome_definition: Historical fisheries collapses (definition not visible).
studies.key_finding: Title-level claim that rising catch variability preceded historical fisheries collapses.
studies.notes: Surfaced only as a title; the Gulf of Alaska community EWS paper the seed referred to (Litzow 2013 GCB) did not surface. Belongs more to the fisheries sweep.

notes: Scope and limits: 59 distinct WebSearch queries run; WebFetch/curl not attempted because the orchestrator stated they are blocked for all relevant publisher/repository domains. All design-field entries are therefore derived from search-result snippets; where snippets did not expose the design detail the field is marked 'unknown' rather than inferred. Key corrections to the orchestrator's brief: (1) Gsell et al. 2016 PNAS used FIVE freshwater ecosystems per PNAS/PubMed/KNAW snippets, not 'nine lakes'; a query for 'nine lakes' Gsell returned only unrelated glacial-lake news. (2) Spanbauer et al. 2016 (body size) is in Proc R Soc B, not Ecosphere. (3) Arani et al. 2021 (exit time) is in Science, not Nature. (4) The Litzow 2013 Global Change Biology Gulf of Alaska paper did not surface; only Litzow 2013 Ecol Appl (Alaska catch variability) appeared. Evidence gaps: Wilkinson 2018's reference-lake design and any false-positive accounting were not visible in any snippet; O'Brien 2023's number of lakes and windowing procedure were not visible; Cline 2014's quantitative results were not visible; the Su 2021 lake name was not visible. Precedents most relevant to the novelty claim (prior work that DID score non-transitioning series or false positives, which the claim must acknowledge): Burthe 2016 (series-level true/false positives; 8%/6% true positives), O'Brien 2023 (true-negative series and chance baseline), Buelo 2022 (true- vs false-positive alarm rates in lake-years with/without enrichment), Drake & Griffen 2010 (30 control populations), Carpenter 2011/Seekell 2012/Batt 2013/Batt 2019 (single reference lake), and Boettiger & Hastings 2012 (prosecutor's fallacy). No study found in this sweep combined sequential fixed-horizon origins, out-of-sample holdout across systems, a matched state/trend forecasting baseline, threshold calibration to a common false-alarm budget, and complete follow-up; Pace 2017 is the only field study with a prospective preset alarm threshold, and it is n=1 lake with no forecasting baseline. Two items surfaced as titles only and warrant follow-up in a later stage: 'Systematically false positives in early warning signal analysis' (PLOS ONE 2019, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0211072) and 'Quantifying limits to detection of early warning for critical transitions' (J R Soc Interface 2012, PubMed 22593100). Per the hard rules, no EWS-outcome associations were computed or speculated about for any candidate dataset.
